_schema: Registry of preferred tools (soft dependencies): the director uses the declared tool when the task matches one of its classes and the tool is available; if unavailable it tells the user — NEVER a silent fallback to an undeclared alternative. This file is yours: the plugin only ADDS entries it ships (soft-deps-template.json) that are missing here, once, and never edits or restores yours.

media-tools.detect: python3 "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/media-doctor.py" (exit 0 = ready): ffmpeg/ffprobe with drawtext, venv ~/.claude/fable-director/tools/venv with faster-whisper + edge-tts, provider gemini-media in cross-family.json
media-tools.cli_zero_token: skill fable-director:analisi-video. 1) video-sheet.sh <file> [--fps 1 | --scenes 0.3] [--out DIR] → ffprobe card + contact sheet with burnt-in timestamps (one Read of the top model); the `audio:` line decides step 2; --scenes gives one frame per cut = shot list at zero cost. 2) transcribe.py <file> [--json --words] → SRT/JSON via faster-whisper small int8 (about 1.1× realtime; --words doubles it); refuses files without an audio track before loading the model. 3) tts-timing.py --file SCRIPT → table label | slot | spoken | delta (edge-tts + ffprobe). 4) media-analyze.py --input V --spec ... --schema-json --type video-shotlist → Gemini generateContent (inline < 19 MB, Files API above): EXTERNAL route, budget-open --route external mandatory; --model gemini-2.5-flash explicit fallback on 503. Sheets and transcripts are cached per file hash (media-cache): same file later = zero seconds.
media-tools.trigger_threshold: ALWAYS ffprobe first: whether there is audio is said by ffprobe, never by a model (Gemini declared speech on a file with no audio track, 2026-09-08). Under ~10 min of total footage: sheets + whisper + top-model reading are the whole job; Gemini only for long footage or many files.
media-tools.unavailable: python3 "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/media-doctor.py" shows what is missing; --setup [--prefetch small] creates the venv and installs (explicit, ~370 MB). Tell the user; never read the video 'by eye' without saying so.
